key_insight: Counterfactual Fairness conclusions can be brittle when based on a single assumed causal graph; CF-GU quantifies how uncertainty in the causal graph affects fairness assessments by evaluating counterfactuals across a distribution of plausible graphs.
problem_solved: Addresses overconfidence in counterfactual fairness audits that assume a single, certain causal graph — providing a way to incorporate causal-structure uncertainty so fairness claims become probabilistic and robust.
method: Bootstrap a causal discovery procedure to generate an ensemble of plausible causal graphs reflecting graph uncertainty.
For each sampled graph, build corresponding structural causal models and compute counterfactual fairness metrics for the target ML model.
Aggregate results across the graph ensemble to produce distributions, confidence intervals, and robustness indicators for fairness assessments.
impact: Enables practitioners to report fairness assessments that reflect epistemic uncertainty about causal structure, reducing false certainty and guiding safer, more informed decisions about model deployment and remediation.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: data → bootstrap causal discovery → ensemble of graphs → per-graph counterfactual evaluation → aggregated fairness distribution
Histogram or violin plot showing distribution of a fairness metric (e.g., counterfactual effect) across sampled graphs with confidence bands
Graph montage: a small set of differing plausible causal graphs highlighting varying edges that most influence fairness outcomes
Heatmap or bar chart labeling decisions/features by robustness (robust vs fragile) indicating where fairness conclusions are stable or uncertain
paper_authors: Davi Valério, Chrysoula Zerva, Mariana Pinto, Ricardo Santos, André Carreiro
